extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent applicants, prosecuting attorneys/agents, and patent examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examiner guidance for preparing, amending, submitting, and handling patent drawings, annotated/ replacement sheets, models, exhibits, specimens, and for detecting/handling new matter in U.S. patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement sheet must include all prior figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Any replacement sheet of drawings shall include all of the figures appearing on the immediate prior version of the sheet, even if only one figure is amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted requirement from 37 CFR 1.121(d). If a drawing figure is to be canceled, the appropriate figure must be removed from the replacement sheet and remaining figures renumbered as necessary; additional replacement sheets may be necessary to show renumbering. The figure or figure number of an amended drawing should not be labeled as 'amended.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Top-margin labeling of drawing sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Each drawing sheet submitted after the filing date of an application must be labeled in the top margin as either 'Replacement Sheet' or 'New Sheet' pursuant to 37 CFR 1.121(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New sheets containing an additional figure must be labeled 'New Sheet.' Replacement sheets must be labeled 'Replacement Sheet' and replacement sheets should be labeled in the page header so as not to obstruct the drawing figures (per 37 CFR 1.84(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of changes in amendment paper
rubrics_metrics.description: All changes to the drawings shall be explained, in detail, in either the drawing amendment or remarks section of the amendment paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A marked-up copy of amended drawings may be included or required; explanations should accompany replacement sheets so the examiner and record understand what changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotated (marked-up) sheets labeling and content
rubrics_metrics.description: A marked-up copy of any amended drawing figure, including annotations indicating the changes made, must be clearly labeled as 'Annotated Sheet' and presented in the amendment or remarks section that explains the change(s) to the drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An annotated sheet may be included by applicant or required by the examiner. Annotated sheets filed by an applicant and used for correction will not be returned. All annotated sheets must be in ink or permanent prints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may require annotated sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: A marked-up copy of any amended drawing figure, including annotations indicating the changes made, must be provided when required by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 6.27 may be used to require a marked-up copy including annotations. If required, the annotated copy must be presented in the amendment or remarks section that explains the change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objections to drawings not held in abeyance
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless applicant is otherwise notified in an Office action, objections to the drawings in a utility or plant application will not be held in abeyance, and a request to hold objections to the drawings in abeyance will not be considered a bona fide attempt to advance the application to final action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.85(a) and MPEP guidance; applicant should not expect objections to be deferred simply by request.

rubrics_metrics.name: If changes not accepted, applicant is notified with corrective action
rubrics_metrics.description: If the changes are not accepted by the examiner, the applicant will be notified and informed of any required corrective action in the next Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The objection to the drawings will not be held in abeyance. The examiner should explicitly and clearly set forth all reasons for not approving corrections in the next communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications must be illustrated; restrictions on broken lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Modifications may not be shown in broken lines on figures which show in solid lines another form of the invention; all modifications described must be illustrated or the text canceled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement does not apply to a mere reference to minor variations nor to well-known and conventional parts. (Cites Ex parte Badger and Ex parte Peck.) Form paragraph 6.22.05 may be used to require correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-art figures usually unnecessary and must be designated
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures showing the prior art are usually unnecessary and should be canceled; however, where needed to understand the invention they may be retained if designated by a legend such as 'Prior Art.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the prior art figure is not labeled, use form paragraph 6.36.01. Replacement drawings in reply to Office action are required to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner review for new matter and entry decision
rubrics_metrics.description: All sheets of replacement drawings will be routinely entered into the contents of the application, but the examiner should consider factors such as new matter, the necessity for the replacement sheets and consistency with other sheets; if the examiner decides not to enter the sheets, provide the applicant with complete, explicit reasoning for the denial of entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries previously made will be marked 'not entered.' Use form paragraph 6.37 to acknowledge replacement drawing sheets, and identify any drawings not entered because they contain new matter and explain corrections necessary to obtain entry upon resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings cannot normally be transferred between pending applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings cannot normally be transferred from a first pending application to another as the Office no longer considers drawings as formal or informal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings that do not comply with all form requirements of 37 CFR 1.84 may nevertheless be acceptable for publication and examination if the drawings are readable and reproducible for publication purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility/plant applications will not be placed on file until drawings objections corrected
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility or plant application will not be placed on the files for examination until objections to the drawings have been corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except as provided in § 1.215(c), any patent application publication will not include drawings filed after the application has been placed on the files for examination. If a drawing in a design application meets certain reproduction requirements it may be admitted even if not fully compliant with § 1.84.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. PTO does not make drawing changes; applicant responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The United States Patent and Trademark Office does not make drawing changes. It is applicant’s responsibility to ensure that the drawings are corrected; corrections must be made in accordance with provided instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs 6.39 (USPTO does not make drawing changes) and 6.40 (Information on how to effect drawing changes) explain that replacement sheets must be presented and changes explained. Use these form paragraphs where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and consequences for corrected drawings (abandonment and deadlines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant is required to submit acceptable corrected drawings within the time period set in the Office action; failure to take corrective action within the set period will result in abandonment of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If corrected drawings are required in a Notice of Allowability (PTOL-37), the new drawings MUST be filed within the THREE MONTH shortened statutory period set for reply in the Notice of Allowability (no extensions under 37 CFR 1.136). If Office of Data Management receives drawings that cannot be scanned or are otherwise unacceptable for publication, they will mail a requirement giving applicant a shortened statutory period of two months to reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canceled figure handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If a drawing figure is canceled, a replacement sheet of drawings must be submitted without the figure. If the canceled drawing figure was the only drawing on the sheet, a marked-up copy of the drawing sheet including an annotation showing that the drawing has been cancelled is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The marked-up (annotated) copy must be clearly labeled 'Annotated Sheet' and presented in the amendment or remarks section which explains the changes. The brief description of the drawings should also be amended to reflect cancellation. A canceled figure may be reinstated by amending the specification adding the brief description of the view if reinstated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotated sheets requirements and retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Annotated sheets filed by an applicant and used for correction of the drawing will not be returned; all such annotated sheets must be in ink or permanent prints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When changes are to be made in the drawing itself (other than mere changes in reference characters, figure designations, or light inking corrections), an annotated copy should be filed. Annotated sheets must be clearly labeled 'Annotated Sheet' and included in the amendment or remarks section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may make minor drawing corrections without applicant annotated sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application is ready for issue except for a slight defect in the drawing not involving change in structure, the examiner may prepare a letter indicating the change and may include a marked-up copy of the drawing showing the addition or alteration; a marked-up copy should be attached to the letter and made of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative corrections that may be suggested without requiring annotated sheets from the applicant include: (A) Adding two or three reference characters or exponents; (B) Changing one or two numerals or figure ordinals; (C) Removing superfluous matter; (D) Adding or reversing directional arrows; (E) Changing Roman numerals to Arabic to agree with specification; (F) Adding section lines or brackets where easily executed; (G) Changing lead lines; (H) Correcting misspelled legends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections entered unless explicitly not accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawing corrections or changes will be entered at the time they are presented, unless applicant is notified to the contrary by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the corrected or changed drawing is not accepted (e.g., because corrections are erroneous, involve new matter, or do not include all necessary corrections), the applicant will be notified and informed of any required corrective action in the next Office action. The examiner should set forth reasons for not approving corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings will not be returned to applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings will not be returned to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotated sheets and replacement sheets filed are retained by the Office; do not expect original drawings to be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: IFW/informal drawings and printing
rubrics_metrics.description: If the drawings submitted in an application have been indicated by the applicant as 'informal', but the drawings are considered acceptable by OPAP, the examiner should not require replacement of the drawings. In IFW applications, generally, the most recently filed drawings will be used for printing unless they have been indicated as 'Not Entered.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner makes an objection to the drawings, the examiner should require correction in reply to the Office action that sets forth the objection. If an application is being allowed and corrected drawings have not been filed, form PTOL-37 provides a check box for requiring corrected drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement drawings after Notice of Allowability handled by Data Management
rubrics_metrics.description: Where replacement drawings are received in utility patent applications after the Notice of Allowability was mailed, the replacement drawings are handled by the Office of Data Management; submission to the examiner is not necessary unless an amendment to the specification accompanies the drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is responsible to ensure no new matter is added when submitting replacement drawings after allowance because they will not normally be reviewed by an examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Models/exhibits/specimens admissibility criteria (37 CFR 1.91)
rubrics_metrics.description: A model or exhibit will not be admitted as part of the record of an application unless it: (1) substantially conforms to the requirements of § 1.52 or § 1.84; (2) is specifically required by the Office; or (3) is filed with a petition under this section including the fee and an explanation of why entry is necessary to demonstrate patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notwithstanding paragraph (a), a model, working model, or other physical exhibit may be required by the Office if deemed necessary for any purpose in examination. Models or exhibits required or submitted with a petition must be accompanied by photographs that show multiple views of the material features and that substantially conform to § 1.84.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographs required for models/exhibits that do not conform
rubrics_metrics.description: If the model or exhibit does not substantially conform to § 1.52 or § 1.84, it must be accompanied by photographs that show multiple views of the material features and substantially conform to the requirements of § 1.84.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material features are those which form the basis for submission. For video or DVD exhibits, applicant must submit photographs of the content (e.g., still frame) and not a photograph of the storage medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Models not ordinarily required; applicant must establish operability if questioned
rubrics_metrics.description: With the exception of cases involving perpetual motion, a model is not ordinarily required by the Office to demonstrate operability of a device. If operability of a device is questioned, the applicant must establish it to the satisfaction of the examiner, but may choose the way of doing so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may require a model or exhibit if necessary for examination, but generally does not demand models for proof of operability except in rare situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling, labeling, and storage of models/exhibits
rubrics_metrics.description: All models and exhibits received by the USPTO should be taken to the Technology Center assigned the related application for examination. The receipt must be recorded on an artifact sheet. A label indicating the application number, filing date, and attorney’s name and address should be attached to the model or exhibit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the model or exhibit cannot be conveniently stored in an artifact folder, it should not be accepted. Models/exhibits may be presented during interviews and should be taken away by applicant or counsel at conclusion; any model left may be disposed of at the Office's discretion unless properly made part of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return and disposal procedures and applicant responsibility for models
rubrics_metrics.description: Models, exhibits, or specimens may be returned to applicant if no longer necessary; when notified, applicant must arrange for return at expense within the time period set to avoid disposal. Applicant is responsible for retaining the actual model/exhibit for the enforceable life of any patent except where exceptions apply (conforming photographs, perishable, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notification will set a time period normally two months from mailing date (shorter for perishables). Extensions of time are available under § 1.136 except for perishables. Failure to arrange return may permit Office to dispose of the item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of exhibits not routinely provided
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of models or other physical exhibits will not ordinarily be furnished by the Office, and any model or exhibit in an application or patent shall not be taken from the Office except in the custody of an employee of the Office specially authorized by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should provide necessary photographs or copies when submitting exhibits if they expect copies to be available for prosecution or external use.

rubrics_metrics.name: No amendment may introduce new matter (35 U.S.C.132 / 37 CFR 1.121)
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment shall introduce new matter into the disclosure of an application; matter not present on the filing date in the specification, claims, or drawings that is added after filing is usually new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If new matter is introduced, the amendment should be objected to under 35 U.S.C.132 and the new matter must be canceled in reply to the Office action. If new matter has been entered into claims or affects the scope of claims, reject claims under 35 U.S.C.112(a) (pre-AIA 112 first paragraph). Replacement drawings containing new matter should not be entered; identify new matter by page/line numbers and explain the examiner's position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples and scope of what may constitute new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: New matter includes not only wholly unsupported additions but also additions like adding specific percentages or compounds after a broader original disclosure, or omission of a step from a method; added characteristics may be inherent and not new matter in some cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See In re Wertheim and MPEP §§ 2163.05-07 for guidance. When in doubt, examiners must be alert to detect new matter; the examiner should clearly identify subject matter considered to be new matter. The holding of new matter may be petitionable or appealable.

rubrics_metrics.name: If originally claimed subject matter capable of illustration is not shown in drawing
rubrics_metrics.description: If subject matter capable of illustration is originally claimed and it is not shown in the drawing, the claim is not rejected but applicant is required to add it to the drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement drawings containing new matter should not be entered; the corrections necessary to obtain entry of the drawing(s) should be explained using form paragraph 6.37.
